identity.name: EMAIL — BEC / Executive Impersonation (Proofpoint TAP + Microsoft 365)
identity.summary: The email_emitter emits Proofpoint TAP messagesDelivered events for a business-email-compromise lure with an executive display-name spoof (classification=impostor) for one recipient, then proves the same impersonation logic fires over the Microsoft 365 EmailEvents shape. Cortex XSIAM raises a BEC/impersonation alert and stitches it to the recipient's identity follow-on.
identity.description: Business email compromise via executive impersonation (T1656) uses a look-alike external sender and a spoofed display name to coerce a recipient into a fraudulent action (wire transfer, gift cards, credential or data hand-off), and can pivot into internal spearphishing (T1534) once a mailbox is trusted. This card drives CortexSim's email_emitter to POST Proofpoint TAP messagesDelivered events (classification=impostor, display_name_spoof set) for ada.lovelace into the email log collector, then repeats the pattern in Microsoft 365 / Defender for Office 365 EmailEvents shape. Detection is email-log analytics in Cortex XSIAM: an XQL rule over the proofpoint_tap_raw dataset flags impostor-classified messages where an external sender carries an executive display name, with a parallel query over the recipient's endpoint/identity follow-on. A correlation rule fuses the impersonation signal with any subsequent anomalous recipient activity into one BEC incident.

prerequisites.description: CortexSim email_emitter EAL plugin registered and an authorized email log collector endpoint reachable.
prerequisites.check_command: python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli describe email_emitter | jq -e '.eal_targets | length > 0'

prerequisites.description: Cortex XSIAM ingesting the Proofpoint TAP (proofpoint_tap_raw) and Microsoft 365 (msft_o365) email datasets.

payload.code:
# Emit a BEC executive-impersonation message (Proofpoint TAP then Microsoft 365 shape).
python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli run /tmp/email-003.yml --live
python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli run /tmp/email-003-m365.yml --live

expected_artifacts.description: Delivered messages from an external sender carrying an executive display-name spoof classified as impostor.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: classification = "impostor" and display_name_spoof = "Chief Executive Officer" for one recipient

expected_artifacts.description: Recipient identity follow-on activity correlated to the impersonation lure.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: recipient identity event within the BEC correlation window

iocs.context: Look-alike external sender domain of the BEC impersonation lure (email_emitter bec_impersonation indicators). Appears in the Proofpoint TAP senderDomain / M365 SenderMailFromDomain field.
Spoofed executive sender address of the BEC lure (email_emitter bec_impersonation indicators). Carries the Chief Executive Officer display-name spoof; pivot for the BEC incident.

biocs.name: EMAIL-003 Pre-Flight email_emitter Metadata Visible
biocs.description: Pre-flight: email_emitter metadata visible to operator. Confirms the EAL plugin is registered and exposes EMAIL targets before any events are emitted, so a null result means a harness fault rather than a detection miss.
biocs.logic:
dataset = proofpoint_tap_raw
| filter messageType in ("messagesBlocked", "messagesDelivered", "clicksPermitted") or _raw_log contains "email_emitter"
| comp count() as preflight_events by recipient
| filter preflight_events >= 0

xql_queries.name: EMAIL-003 BEC Executive Impersonation Display-Name Spoof
xql_queries.query:
// [MODEL: dataset=proofpoint_tap_raw, content_id="ProofpointTAP"]
dataset = proofpoint_tap_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter classification = "impostor" and messageType = "messagesDelivered"
| comp count() as bec_events, values(sender) as senders, values(display_name_spoof) as spoofed_names by recipient
| filter bec_events >= 1
| fields recipient, senders, spoofed_names, bec_events

xql_queries.name: EMAIL-003 BEC Recipient Endpoint Follow-On Stitch
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS
| comp count() as endpoint_events, values(action_process_image_name) as procs by actor_effective_username
| filter endpoint_events >= 1
| fields actor_effective_username, endpoint_events, procs

correlation_rules.name: BEC Executive Impersonation — Email to Identity Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: XQL(EMAIL-003 BEC Executive Impersonation Display-Name Spoof) FOLLOWED_BY msft_o365 mailbox-rule change OR xdr_data endpoint activity for the same recipient within 4h

analytics_modules: Cortex XSIAM Email Analytics — Impostor display-name spoof from external sender
Cortex XSIAM Correlation — BEC lure to recipient identity follow-on stitch

products.evidence_query: dataset = proofpoint_tap_raw | filter classification = "impostor" | comp count() by recipient | filter _count >= 1
Correlation CR-EMAIL-0003 fuses the BEC impersonation lure with the recipient's identity follow-on into one BEC incident.

use_cases.name: BEC / Executive Impersonation Detection
use_cases.description: Detect an executive display-name spoof from an external sender across both Proofpoint TAP and Microsoft 365 email log shapes, stitched to the recipient identity follow-on.

test_cases.objective: An impostor-classified message with an executive display-name spoof raises a BEC alert.
preconditions: Cortex XSIAM ingesting proofpoint_tap_raw and msft_o365 datasets.
email_emitter authorized against the lab collector.
steps: Observe the BEC/impersonation alert per recipient in the Cortex console.
success_criteria: XQL `EMAIL-003 BEC Executive Impersonation Display-Name Spoof` returns >= 1 row.

test_cases.objective: The BEC lure stitches to the recipient identity follow-on.
success_criteria: Correlation `CR-EMAIL-0003` groups the impersonation lure with the recipient identity follow-on under one incident.

preventive_controls: Enforce DMARC reject and external-sender display-name warning banners.
Require out-of-band verification for payment / wire-transfer requests.
Block look-alike and newly-registered sender domains targeting executives.
detection_engineering: Flag external senders carrying an internal executive display name (display-name spoof).
Normalize Proofpoint TAP impostor classifications and Microsoft 365 EmailEvents into one schema.
Stitch the BEC lure to the recipient's identity / mailbox-rule follow-on.
